feedback: Revise. This candidate is identical to the design raced in iteration 8 (kd 0.2, kp 2.0, ki 0.3, base_speed 1.0, search_right, sensor_size 0.012, same x positions). That race scored 69.031, below the best raced design, iteration 5 (75.779, kd 0.1). Against iteration 5, progress fell on every track (oval 0.29 to 0.27, s-bend 0.15 to 0.137, slalom 0.11 to 0.089), and steering_oscillation rose on the oval from 0.16 to 0.17. Raising kd did not reduce max_error, which stayed at about 0.062 m on every track, so damping is not the limit and kd 0.2 should not be kept. Iteration 6 (kp 1.6) and iteration 7 (sensor_size 0.016) also lost progress, so kp 2.0 and sensor_size 0.012 stay. Revise so the next race tests speed alone on the best gains. Read the next race this way: if progress on the bend tracks (s-bend, slalom) rises above iteration 5 while the oval holds near 0.29, keep base_speed 1.1 and consider a further step. If the oval progress falls or line_loss_events rises, return base_speed to 1.0 and accept iteration 5 as the best gain set. Iterations 3 and 4 showed that speed shifts progress between the oval and the bend tracks, so 1.1 is a small step to test that trade-off.
requested_changes: Set controller.kd back to 0.1 (iteration 5 value, score 75.779). Iteration 8 with kd 0.2 scored 69.031, with lower progress on all three tracks and higher oscillation on the oval (0.17 vs 0.16).

Set controller.base_speed to 1.1, keeping kp 2.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, search_right, sensor_size 0.012 and the iteration 5 sensor positions. Iterations 3 and 4 showed speed moves progress between the oval and the bend tracks, so 1.1 is a small test of whether bend progress can rise without losing the oval.

Do not change kp, sensor_size or sensor positions in this revision. Iterations 6 and 7 showed that kp 1.6 and sensor_size 0.016 both lowered progress, so the next race should isolate base_speed on the best gain set.
